samples: This module gives you a simple last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, size and emptiness checks) that never changes a stack in place, returning a new one each time, and popping or peeking an empty stack gives "nothing" rather than an error. It also provides a `balanced` function that checks whether round and square brackets in a piece of text are closed in the correct order, ignoring all other characters. It is pure, with no external access, and it includes examples and tests, so it is a safe and small building block for bracket validation or for general stack use.

This module gives you a generic last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, size and emptiness checks) in which every operation returns a new stack instead of changing the old one, and popping or peeking an empty stack gives "nothing" rather than failing. It also provides a pure function that checks whether the round and square brackets in a piece of text are closed in the correct order, ignoring all other characters. It needs no permissions, and it includes examples and tests, so it is a safe, self-contained building block for bracket validation or for any code that needs a simple stack.

This module provides a simple immutable last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, plus a size and emptiness check), where push and pop return new stacks rather than changing the old one. On top of it, it offers a checker that says whether the round `()` and square `[]` brackets in a piece of text are closed in the right order, ignoring all other characters, including curly braces, which are not checked. It is pure, with no file, network, or console access, and it comes with examples and tests, so it is safe to drop in if those are the only bracket kinds you need.

This module provides a simple last-in first-out stack, an immutable one: pushing and popping return new stacks rather than changing the old one. It also supplies size and emptiness checks, plus a `balanced` function that tells you whether the round `()` and square `[]` brackets in a piece of text are properly paired and nested. It is pure (no I/O or other effects), and the `balanced` examples and the stack tests cover the main cases, including empty and mismatched input.

This module provides a simple last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, and a size/emptiness check) that never changes a stack in place and instead returns updated copies, with pop and peek giving "nothing" when the stack is empty. It also offers a `balanced` function that checks whether the round and square brackets in a piece of text are closed in the correct order, ignoring all other characters. It is pure (needs no permissions) and comes with examples and tests, so it looks safe to adopt for basic stack or bracket-matching needs, though it does not handle curly braces.
